thread:
selena: Heads-up: we're rolling out the graceful-degradation-v3 policy in us-central during a maintenance window on Mon 10/20 01:00-02:00 UTC. This policy changes how we shed non-critical work and throttle tokens to keep customer 5xxs low. It's a controlled rollout + dry-run of the live switch. Please ack if you own any affected services. :mega:

mike: Ack. Which services are affected?

selena: Affected: inference-gateway, routing-layer, telemetry-ingest (non-critical). Not affected: billing, auth. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/eng-sre/graceful-degrade-v3. Main steps: preflight -> dry-run canary -> staged enable (5%/25%/100%) -> monitor -> rollback if needed.

kevin: I'll handle the routing-layer changes. Preflight checklist?

selena: Preflight (short):
```
# verify feature flag exists
redwood-admin features get graceful-degradation-v3 --region us-central
# snapshot current SLOs and tokens
redwood-slo snapshot --region us-central --out /tmp/slo-snap.json
# check KV lag & cache health
redwood-metrics query "kv_replication_lag{region=\\"us-central\\"}"
```

ops-bot: Calendar invite created: "US-CENTRAL graceful-degrade-v3 rollout (dry-run)" Mon 10/20 01:00-02:00 UTC. Attendees: eng-sre, eng-runtime, obs. Preflight job scheduled at 00:40 UTC.

oncall: I'm oncall for that window. If customer 5xxs >0.2% or p99 >2x we pause. Who's owning telemetry checks?

mike: I'll own telemetry checks and dashboards. I'll add an alert-suppression for internal pagers but keep external notifications.

selena: Starting dry-run canary at 01:05 with 2% traffic (dry-run mode: sim only). Command: `redwood-degrade plan --policy graceful-degradation-v3 --region us-central --dry-run=true --canary=2%`

pager-bot: Dry-run canary simulated at 01:05. Synthetic metrics injected.

kevin: Canary report: latency p95 +7ms, synthetic errors 0 -> passes smoke tests. No propagation issues.

selena: Proceeding to staged enable (real toggle) at 01:20: 5% traffic target. Keep monitoring.

ops-bot: Feature flag toggled for 5% at 01:20. Job ID: rollout-200123-1

oncall: Observed a small uptick in telemetry ingestion queue depth after 5% switch, but customer-facing latencies stable. Pausing briefly to verify KV warmup.

mike: Looking at logs: a mis-tagged routing rule sent ~0.5% of control traffic to the degrade path incorrectly. Fixing rule now. Patch: `routingctl update-rule --id r-234 --remove-tag test-only`.

kevin: Patch applied. Replaying delayed control traffic. Post-fix: queue drained, telemetry queue depth normalized.

ops-bot: Rollout paused for 4m during fix. Resuming staged enable to 25% at 01:30.

selena: Staged to 25% at 01:30. Monitoring p95/p99 and error-rate.

pager-bot: Internal pager suppression active for window. External alerts remain.

kevin: At 25% we saw a brief token spike tied to client-side retries (duration ~90s). Mitigation: temporary token-throttle at edge (cap 1.8x baseline) while clients backoff.

oncall: Token-throttle applied. Observed client retry reduction; token rate normalized. No customer 5xxs.

selena: Proceed to 100% at 01:45. If anyone wants to stop, call it now.

mike: Go for it.

ops-bot: Staged enable to 100% complete at 01:46. Post-checks running.

kevin: Post-checks: p95 within +12ms, p99 within +20ms, customer 5xxs = 0.01%. Looks healthy.

selena: Great. Leaving SLO annotation for 30m cooldown. We'll keep internal burn leniency but will file a short postmortem. Action items: 1) kevin: add rule-gating test to CI; 2) mike: add telemetry queue synthetic for staged toggles; 3) selena: update runbook with throttling knobs and rollback steps.

oncall: I'll prepare a short postmortem and timeline for the runbook. If any customer impact shows up in the next 30m I'll escalate.

slo-bot: SLO annotation applied: graceful-degrade-v3 rollout us-central. Internal leniency tag active until 02:16 UTC.

selena: Thanks everyone. Please ack action items and whether you can take ownership. Quick sync 15m before the next regional rollout. :raised_hands:
